newsitem.title: USA: Georgetown, S.C., to vote on $107 mln school GOs.
newsitem.headline: Georgetown, S.C., to vote on $107 mln school GOs.

text.p: South Carolina's Georgetown County has scheduled a May 20 referendum on a $107 million general obligation bond issue for schools, district spokeswoman Rosemary Amaker said Thursday.
The proposal would raise property taxes by $80 a year on a $100,000 home. If the referendum passes, the 20-year bonds would be issued next fall, Amaker said.

Voters rejected a $108.84 million GO bond issue for schools in a May 1995 referendum by a narrow margin. Amaker said the ballot in the election was confusing, with the bond proposal following two pages of school board nominations.
"Many people didn't know there was a third page," Amakur said.

Another $98 million GO proposal for schools was stricken last year by the U.S. Justice Department because of questions over desegregation. It would have left the county with one all-black high school, something the current plan eliminates.
"This one has been cleared" by the department, Amaker said.
The bonds would be sold by competitive bid, she said.
